 KrisFlyer Scoot Singapore Airlines Spontaneous Escapes Singapore Airlines and Scoot KrisFlyer Spontaneous Escapes for December 2026
 by Andrew 16 November 2026, 12:00 16 November 2026, 12:00 
 Leave a Comment on Singapore Airlines and Scoot KrisFlyer Spontaneous Escapes for December 2026 
 KrisFlyer’s Spontaneous Escapes deal is back for December 2026, with 30% off Singapore Airlines awards and 15% off Scoot.
Here’s our full list with aircraft and seat types, interactive maps, and our top picks this month. 
 KrisFlyer has launched its monthly Spontaneous Escapes promotion for December 2026, offering discounts of 30% on Singapore Airlines Economy, Premium Economy, and Business Class award bookings to and from a selection of destinations across its network, plus 15% off Economy awards on selected Scoot flights.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 As usual, to take advantage of the savings you’ll need to secure your tickets within the next two weeks, though the sooner the better is a good plan, since award seats at these discounted rates are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
 If any of the destinations on this month’s list catch your eye and you’re able to make firm travel plans for next month, it’s definitely worth seizing the opportunity to book one of these seats at the discounted rate.
 (Image: Singapore Airlines) 
 Singapore Airlines awards start at 5,600 miles one-way in Economy Class, between Singapore and the likes of Bali, Kuala Lumpur or Surabaya, while Scoot awards start at just 1,275 miles one-way on Singapore – Malaysia routes like Ipoh, Kuantan and Langkawi.
 Our picks for December 2026
 Some of the best deals worth considering this month to or from Singapore, on both Singapore Airlines and Scoot, are outlined below.

 ADVERTISEMENT 
 If you do find a route of interest, you’ll need to book these ‘Promo’ awards over the next two weeks – between 16th November 2026 and 30th November 2026 – for travel in December 2026, but remember there’s no flexibility and no refunds are allowed.
 Spontaneous Escapes map
 Once again this month we’ve produced a map of SIA’s Spontaneous Escapes destinations for December 2026, which also allows you to filter by cabin class, zoom in on particular regions, and easily see blackout dates for the city of your choice.
 Scoot’s Spontaneous Escapes destinations for December 2026 have their own map too, shown below.
 Business Class Deals
 As always, we’re the only site showing the aircraft type and the Business Class seat product planned for these routes flight number by flight number, to help you choose better and travel smarter on your discounted Spontaneous Escapes getaway.

 Are the Scoot deals worth it?
 Since April 2026, the Spontaneous Escapes deal includes Scoot flights, made possible since the carrier adopted a fixed-price award chart for KrisFlyer redemptions.
 Scoot cash fares are often very competitive though, even at short notice, and you still pay taxes and fees on an award ticket, so a discounted rate isn’t automatically a good deal.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 The sum is simple enough. Take the cash fare, subtract the taxes and fees you’d pay on the award anyway, and divide what’s left by the number of miles needed. That tells you what each mile is actually earning you.
 Rather than doing the sums yourself, pop the figures into our calculator below for a quick answer.
 Is it worth it?

 Selecting a promo award on flyscoot.com brings up a quote as miles plus cash, for example 1,500 miles + S$65.20, and that cash figure is the taxes and fees. Both that and the cash fare assume a Basic fare, so compare like with like if you need bags or a seat.
 Tool by mainlymiles.com 
 As a rough guide, anything under 1 cent per mile is worse than simply cashing your miles out through Kris+ or KrisShop, so it isn’t worth doing even if your miles are about to expire.
 Between 1 cent and 1.5 cents you’re in territory KrisFlyer cash-out promotions will sometimes match. Above 1.5 cents you’re doing better than you can usually cash out for, and at 2 cents and above it’s a redemption worth making.
 Bear in mind Singapore Airlines redemptions, particularly in the premium cabins and particularly at Spontaneous Escapes rates, will usually value your miles more highly than a Scoot Economy seat will – so if you’re sitting on a decent non-expiring balance and have no fixed plans, that’s almost always the better use for them.
 Scoot awards using KrisFlyer miles are always non-refundable year-round, so there is no loss of flexibility when booking a Spontaneous Escapes award on these flights for December 2026, since you always need to be committed to these ‘use them or lose them’ redemptions on the low-cost carrier anyway.
 Terms and conditions
 Here are the terms and conditions for the Spontaneous Escapes promotion.
 December 2026 offer
 A 30% discount on SIA saver award redemptions for travel to and/or from selected destinations in December 2026.
 A 15% discount on Scoot Economy saver award redemptions for travel to and/or from selected destinations in December 2026.
 Redeem Scoot flights online at flyscoot.com or via the Scoot mobile app, between 16th November 2026 9am (SGT) and 30th November 2026 11.59pm (SGT).
 Redeem SIA flights online at singaporeair.com or via the SingaporeAir mobile app, between 16th November 2026 9am (SGT) and 30th November 2026 11.59pm (SGT).
 Travel must commence no earlier than 1st December 2026 and be completed by 31st December 2026.
 Flights are non-refundable and non-changeable.
 Blackout dates apply on some routes (see the full lists above for details).
 Book one-way legs if the discount only applies on one of the two (or more) flight numbers you need. You cannot book one-way Promo (Spontaneous Escapes) and one-way Saver / Advantage awards in the same booking.
 Book as many redemptions as you like at Spontaneous Escapes rates – it’s not capped.
 You cannot waitlist for Promo (Spontaneous Escapes) redemptions.
 Requests to change any booking details, or to retain the ticket for future use, will not be granted.
 In a nutshell – be sure to have firm travel plans if you’re locking in a Spontaneous Escapes deal.
 Book the ‘Promo’ award category
 Singapore Airlines and Scoot offer the Spontaneous Escapes deals under their “Promo” award category, which you’ll see alongside the usual Saver, Advantage and Access award rates on applicable flights.
 If the Promo award rate is not shown for your preferred flight, even though it is listed as part of the offer, that unfortunately means there is no availability remaining at the Spontaneous Escapes rate (but do check back later, like Saver and Advantage award space – it can come and go).
 The “Promo” award category also means Spontaneous Escapes award capacity can be loaded as a subset of the Saver award space. This allows you to continue to book at Saver rates (if you prefer the flexibility, for example), or allows the airline to stop offering Spontaneous Escapes rates on a particular flight, while not necessarily having to remove the Saver rate at the same time, like they did under the previous system.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 This also opens up the possibility of securing discounted bookings for larger groups.
 For example, if three of you are traveling but only two Promo (Spontaneous Escapes) award seats are available for your desired flight, you can potentially redeem the two available Promo seats and then one Saver seat on a separate booking.
 This way, you can still effectively enjoy a 20% overall mileage discount across your group, compared to booking three regular-rate Saver awards.
 What if you already booked?
 If you have already redeemed your miles on a Singapore Airlines flight that has now become eligible for the Spontaneous Escapes offer, unfortunately there’s no simple way to change it and pay the reduced miles rate.
 You will have to book again at the Spontaneous Escapes rate, then cancel the existing booking and pay the miles redeposit fee (don’t do it the other way round, in case the Spontaneous Escapes Promo space disappears in the meantime!).
 This will require you to have sufficient miles in your account to immediately lock in the Spontaneous Escapes rate.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 If you need the miles from the original booking in order to make the Spontaneous Escapes one due to an insufficient balance, be very careful !
 Since you will first have to cancel the original booking, you are now at the mercy of the Spontaneous Escapes space remaining available on the flight, and it can sometimes take a few days for the miles from your original cancelled booking to be re-credited to your account.
 Full details
 For full details of this month’s Spontaneous Escapes offer, including terms and conditions (but sadly not including the aircraft type and seat type details we have provided above!), head over to the KrisFlyer Spontaneous Escapes promo page .
 Scoot’s Spontaneous awards list, meanwhile, is available here .
 Summary
 KrisFlyer’s regular monthly Spontaneous Escapes deal is back for travel in December 2026, for those who can make short-term travel plans.
 Good offers in Business Class include Adelaide, Melbourne (on the A380) and Western Sydney for 50,400 miles , Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City, Phnom Penh and Phuket for 17,500 miles and Bali for 15,400 miles .
 In Economy, the standouts are Europe and the US West Coast at 30,800 miles , including London, Paris, Milan and Los Angeles, with Australia from 20,300 miles and Perth or Darwin even lower at 14,350 miles . Bangkok and Phuket for 9,100 miles and Bali for 5,600 miles are also decent rates.
 Selected Scoot flights are part of the deal again this month, at 15% off rather than 30%, but that still means award tickets from just 1,275 miles one-way on Malaysia routes like Ipoh, Kuantan and Langkawi.
 There are no North Asia destinations on SIA this month, but Scoot helps fill the gap with plenty of China options from 10,200 miles . It also offers Perth for 5,525 miles and Melbourne or Sydney for 10,625 miles , well below SIA’s rates.

 Remember if you’re unable to secure a return flight at the discounted rates, book two one-way tickets instead. You’ll pay the ‘Promo’ rate one-way and the usual ‘Saver’ rate for the non-discounted sector, but at least the whole itinerary will not be at the usual rate (and half the discount is still welcome).
